ApiPhloHelpers

Documentation / API / phlo / helpers

Public lakehouse helper utilities for Phlo workflow authors.

The helpers in this package are deliberately small, dependency-light building blocks. They compose the existing Phlo capability system while staying useful in plain unit tests and notebooks.

synthetic_key

Render a deterministic SHA-256 synthetic row-key SQL expression.

The rendered expression is part of Phlo's compatibility contract: for a given supported dialect, namespace, field order, and field values, Phlo will preserve the canonical payload semantics across releases. Each field is tagged as null or value, non-null values are cast with dialect-stable string casts, and values are length-prefixed before hashing so adjacent fields cannot collide by concatenation.

deduplicate_arrow_by_unique_key

Deduplicate rows sharing the same unique-key value within one batch.

Applies deterministic, batch-local deduplication on a PyArrow Table so that delete-then-append merge paths never leave duplicate keys behind.

Semantics:

  • method="last" keeps, per key, the row with the greatest order_by value. order_by must be provided; Parquet row order is never used as an implicit tiebreaker.
  • method="first" keeps the first occurrence of each key in input order.
  • Rows without duplicate keys are returned unchanged (identity on key).

Parameters

NameTypeDefaultDescription
arrow_table--PyArrow Table to deduplicate.
unique_keystr-Column identifying distinct entities.
methodstr-Deduplication strategy, first or last.
order_by`strNone`-

Returns

tuple — (deduplicated_table, duplicates_removed_count).

Raises

  • ValueError — If the method is unsupported, or order_by is missing or absent from the data where required.

Submodules

  • artifacts — Generic artifact manifest helpers.
  • backfills — Backfill planning helpers.
  • bitemporal — Bitemporal scope and SQL predicate helpers.
  • connections — Connection resolution and representation helpers.
  • crosswalks — Generic cross-system identity mapping helpers.
  • effective — Effective-dated reference data helpers.
  • errors — Error handling helpers for workflow code.
  • events — Generic event-ledger helpers.
  • evidence — Evidence summary helpers for governed workflow outputs.
  • governance — Governance, policy, and audit helper utilities.
  • incremental — Incremental load and watermark helpers.
  • ingestion — General ingestion helper utilities.
  • io — Read and write convenience helpers for workflow authors.
  • lineage — Lineage helper utilities.
  • maintenance — Maintenance policy helpers for lakehouse tables.
  • observability — Observability and alerting helpers for workflow code.
  • partitions — Partition key and partition-scope helpers.
  • publishing — Publish target helper utilities.
  • quality — Quality helper factories and checks that do not require a provider import.
  • reconciliation — Reconciliation helpers for comparing source and target datasets.
  • references — Reference-data contract helpers.
  • schema — Normalized schema construction helpers.
  • sql — Small SQL construction and safety helpers.
  • states — Generic state-transition validation helpers.
  • storage — Object-store path and layout helpers.
  • supersession — Helpers for corrected, superseded, and latest-view records.
  • tables — Provider-neutral table naming and table-store helpers.
  • testing — Testing helpers for lightweight workflow unit tests.
  • wap — Write-audit-publish helper primitives.
